content.text: create a simple 3d game in a single self-contained html page, feel free to use http-loaded dependencies/libraries from unpkg/etc.

* Goal: Simple 3D game. * Format: Single self-contained HTML page. * Dependencies: Allowed (via CDN like unpkg). * Constraint: Must be "simple" but functional. * Three.js is the gold standard for 3D in the browser. It's powerful, well-documented, and easy to load via CDN. * A "3D Runner" or "Obstacle Avoidance" game is classic, easy to implement, and visually rewarding. * *Concept:* A cube (player) moves forward on a track; avoid red blocks; collect gold coins (or just survive as long as possible). Let's go with a "Cube Runner" where you avoid obstacles. * *Basic Setup:* Scene, Camera, Renderer. * *Player:* A cube. * *Environment:* A long plane/ground. * *Obstacles:* Randomly spawned boxes that move toward the player. * *Controls:* Left/Right arrow keys or A/D. * *Game Loop:* `requestAnimationFrame`, updating positions, collision detection. * *UI:* Score counter and Game Over screen. * *HTML Structure:* ```html ...style...
Score: 0
Press Start
``` * *Three.js Boilerplate:* * `scene = new THREE.Scene()` * `camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(...)` * `renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer()` * Add some lights (Ambient + Directional). * *Game Logic Details:* * *Player Movement:* Use a target X position and lerp (linear interpolation) or just snap to lanes to make it feel snappy. Let's go with smooth movement. * *Obstacle Spawning:* Every X frames, create a mesh at the end of the track and give it a negative Z velocity. * *Collision:* Use `Box3` (Three.js built-in) for simple AABB collision detection. * *Speed Ramp:* Increase speed over time to make it challenging. * *Styling:* Dark background, neon colors for the player and obstacles to give it a "synthwave" feel. * *Performance:* Dispose of obstacles once they pass the player to prevent memory leaks. * *Self-contained?* Yes. * *3D?* Yes (Three.js). * *Simple?* Yes. * (Self-Correction during coding): Make sure the camera follows the player or the world moves. It's easier to keep the player at Z=0 and move the world toward them. * Add a "Restart" button. * Ensure responsive canvas resizing. * Add a simple "Score" tracker.
